sentences.text: Amanzia is a genus of turiasaurian sauropod dinosaur found in the Late Jurassic Reuchenette Formation in Moutier, Switzerland.
This animal belongs to the family Turiasauria.
It holds the distinction of being the first sauropod dinosaur named from remains discovered in Switzerland.
Researchers noted the rare preservation of fossilized cartilage within a limb joint.
The genus name Amanzia was established in 2020 by Schwarz et al. in honor of Amanz Gressly, the first person to discover dinosaur bones in Switzerland.
After cleaning and preparation in 2003, it was realized that the fossils were not closely related to Cetiosauriscus.
The fossil bones are not articulated, are strongly compressed, and were often damaged during removal from the rock.
While von Huene originally thought the material represented two or three individuals, a 2020 study concluded there were at least four individuals.
Among the four individuals, two are similar in size, one is 15% longer, and one is 20% shorter.
In 2020, seventy-five additional sauropod specimens from the same site were referred to the species Amanzia greppini.
The fossils date to the Kimmeridgian stage, between 152.7 and 152 million years ago.
The time range for Amanzia is the Kimmeridgian, from 154.8 to 152.21 million years ago.
